item.description: The beautiful and mercenary Honey is a monstrously compelling character, in a novel with the ruthlessness of Richard Yates but more wit ‘A sweet white grape of a book” is how Virginia Woolf described Elizabeth Jenkins’s first novel, Virginia Water, published in 1929 when Jenkins was 24. Jenkins may have detected a condescending note. She was wary of Woolf, having been invited into the Bloomsbury inner circle and then (in her own view, at least) just as quickly dropped again. Jenkins soon regretted the novel’s publication, apparently afraid acquaintances might recognise themselves, and tried to get rid of as many copies as she could. Fortunately she wasn’t long deterred, either by her uneasy dealings with Woolf or her anxiety about Virginia Water; her subsequent literary career spanned 70 years, though most of her books had fallen out of print by the time she died in 2010. I noticed that she wasn’t wearing a collar. I thought to myself, that dog clearly doesn’t belong there – she needs help. Why is she out on her own?
